cohort: 70 women with multiple sclerosis who delivered at the University Hospital Brno from 2004 to 2013
finding: There was no significant difference in the rate of multiple sclerosis relapse at 6 months postpartum between women who had vaginal deliveries and caesarean sections, or between those who did and did not receive different types of obstetric analgesia/anaesthesia.
mod_finding: Neither delivery mode (vaginal vs Caesarean) nor type of obstetric anesthesia/analgesia were found to have any impact on the course of MS at 6 months postpartum.
